verse_count_notes: 28 numbered verses plus the traditional concluding half-verse (28½); represented as 29 text units so the closing half-verse is retained explicitly.

verses.sanskrit: द्रव्यमेव रसादीनां श्रेष्ठं ते हि तदाश्रयाः । पञ्चभूतात्मकं तत्तु क्ष्मामधिष्ठाय जायते ॥१॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 1 establishes the primacy of dravya, its Panchamahabhuta basis, and why substances have multiple elemental and doshic associations.

verses.sanskrit: अम्बुयोन्यग्निपवननभसां समवायतः । तन्निर्वृत्तिर्विशेषश्च व्यपदेशस्तु भूयसा ॥२॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 2 establishes the primacy of dravya, its Panchamahabhuta basis, and why substances have multiple elemental and doshic associations.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मान्नैकरसं द्रव्यं भूतसङ्घातसम्भवात् । नैकदोषास्ततो रोगास्तत्र व्यक्तो रसः स्मृतः ॥३॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 3 establishes the primacy of dravya, its Panchamahabhuta basis, and why substances have multiple elemental and doshic associations.

verses.sanskrit: तन्नैकभूतजं द्रव्यमव्यक्तोऽनुरसः किञ्चिदन्ते व्यक्तोऽपि चेष्यते । गुर्वादयो गुणा द्रव्ये पृथिव्यादौ रसाश्रये ॥४॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 4 explains the elemental predominance and characteristic qualities, actions and movement of parthiva, apya, agneya, vayavya and nabhasa substances.

verses.sanskrit: रसेषु व्यपदिश्यन्ते साहचर्योपचारतः । तत्र द्रव्यं गुरुस्थूलस्थिरगन्धगुणोल्बणम् ॥५॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 5 explains the elemental predominance and characteristic qualities, actions and movement of parthiva, apya, agneya, vayavya and nabhasa substances.

verses.sanskrit: पार्थिवं गौरवस्थैर्यसङ्घातोपचयावहम् । द्रवशीतगुरुस्निग्धमन्दसान्द्ररसोल्बणम् ॥६॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 6 explains the elemental predominance and characteristic qualities, actions and movement of parthiva, apya, agneya, vayavya and nabhasa substances.

verses.sanskrit: आप्यं स्नेहनविष्यन्दक्लेदप्रह्लादबन्धकृत् । रूक्षतीक्ष्णोष्णविशदरूपगुणोल्बणम् ॥७॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 7 explains the elemental predominance and characteristic qualities, actions and movement of parthiva, apya, agneya, vayavya and nabhasa substances.

verses.sanskrit: आग्नेयं दाहभावर्णप्रकाशपवनात्मकम् । वायव्यं रूक्षविशदलघुस्पर्शगुणोल्बणम् ॥८॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 8 explains the elemental predominance and characteristic qualities, actions and movement of parthiva, apya, agneya, vayavya and nabhasa substances.

verses.sanskrit: रौक्ष्यलाघववैशद्यविचारग्लानिकारकम् । नाभसं सूक्ष्मविशदलघुशब्दगुणोल्बणम् ॥९॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 9 explains the elemental predominance and characteristic qualities, actions and movement of parthiva, apya, agneya, vayavya and nabhasa substances.

verses.sanskrit: सौषिर्यलाघवकरं जगत्येवनौषधम् । न किञ्चिद्विद्यते द्रव्यं वशान्नानार्थयोगयोः ॥१०॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 10 explains the elemental predominance and characteristic qualities, actions and movement of parthiva, apya, agneya, vayavya and nabhasa substances.

verses.sanskrit: द्रव्यमूर्ध्वगतं तत्र प्रायोऽग्निपवनोत्कटम् । अधोगामि च भूयिष्ठं भूमितोयगुणाधिकम् ॥११॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 11 explains the elemental predominance and characteristic qualities, actions and movement of parthiva, apya, agneya, vayavya and nabhasa substances.

verses.sanskrit: इति द्रव्यं रसान्भेदैरुत्तरत्रोपदेक्ष्यते । वीर्यं पुनर्वदन्त्येके गुरुस्निग्धं हिमं मृदु ॥१२॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 12 explains virya, competing classical definitions, the eightfold quality-based interpretation, and the two principal expressions of virya as ushna and shita.

verses.sanskrit: लघु रूक्षोष्णतीक्ष्णं च तद्वदेवाष्टधा मतम् । चरकस्त्वाह वीर्यं तत्क्रियते येन या क्रिया ॥१३॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 13 explains virya, competing classical definitions, the eightfold quality-based interpretation, and the two principal expressions of virya as ushna and shita.

verses.sanskrit: नावीर्यं कुरुते किञ्चित्सर्वा वीर्यकृता हि सा । गुर्वादिष्वेव वीर्याख्या तेनान्वर्थेति वर्ण्यते ॥१४॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 14 explains virya, competing classical definitions, the eightfold quality-based interpretation, and the two principal expressions of virya as ushna and shita.

verses.sanskrit: समग्रगुणसारेषु शक्त्युत्कर्षविवर्तिषु । व्यवहाराय मुख्यत्वाद्बह्वग्रग्रहणादपि ॥१५॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 15 explains virya, competing classical definitions, the eightfold quality-based interpretation, and the two principal expressions of virya as ushna and shita.

verses.sanskrit: अतश्च विपरीतत्वात्सम्भवन्त्यपि नैव सा । विवक्ष्यते रसाद्येषु वीर्यं गुर्वादयो ह्यतः ॥१६॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 16 explains virya, competing classical definitions, the eightfold quality-based interpretation, and the two principal expressions of virya as ushna and shita.

verses.sanskrit: उष्णं शीतं द्विधैवान्ये वीर्यमाचक्षतेऽपि च । नानात्मकमपि द्रव्यमग्नीषोमौ महाबलौ ॥१७॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 17 explains virya, competing classical definitions, the eightfold quality-based interpretation, and the two principal expressions of virya as ushna and shita.

verses.sanskrit: व्यक्ताव्यक्तं जगदिव नातिक्रामति जातुचित् । तत्रोष्णं भ्रमतृड्ग्लानिस्वेददाहाशुपाकिताः ॥१८॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 18 explains virya, competing classical definitions, the eightfold quality-based interpretation, and the two principal expressions of virya as ushna and shita.

verses.sanskrit: शमं च वातकफयोः करोति शिशिरं पुनः । ह्लादनं जीवनं स्तम्भं प्रसादं रक्तपित्तयोः ॥१९॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 19 explains virya, competing classical definitions, the eightfold quality-based interpretation, and the two principal expressions of virya as ushna and shita.

verses.sanskrit: जाठरेणाग्निना योगाद्यदुदेति रसान्तरम् । रसानां परिणामान्ते स विपाक इति स्मृतः ॥२०॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 20 defines vipaka as the final post-digestive transformation and explains its principal threefold classification.

verses.sanskrit: स्वादुः पटुश्च मधुरमम्लोऽम्लं पच्यते रसः । तिक्तोषणकषायाणां विपाकः प्रायशः कटुः ॥२१॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 21 defines vipaka as the final post-digestive transformation and explains its principal threefold classification.

verses.sanskrit: रसैरसौ तुल्यफलस्तत्र द्रव्यं शुभाशुभम् । किञ्चिद्रसेन कुरुते कर्म पाकेन चापरम् ॥२२॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 22 explains how rasa, vipaka, virya and prabhava contribute to the action of a substance and the hierarchy of their relative strength.

verses.sanskrit: गुणान्तरेण वीर्येण प्रभावेणैव किञ्चन । यद्यद्द्रव्ये रसादीनां बलवत्त्वेन वर्तते ॥२३॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 23 explains how rasa, vipaka, virya and prabhava contribute to the action of a substance and the hierarchy of their relative strength.

verses.sanskrit: अभिभूयेतरांस्तत्तत्कारणत्वं प्रपद्यते । विरुद्धगुणसंयोगे भूयसाल्पं हि जीयते ॥२४॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 24 explains how rasa, vipaka, virya and prabhava contribute to the action of a substance and the hierarchy of their relative strength.

verses.sanskrit: रसं विपाकस्तौ वीर्यं प्रभावस्तान्यपोहति । बलसाम्ये रसादीनामिति नैसर्गिकं बलम् ॥२५॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 25 explains how rasa, vipaka, virya and prabhava contribute to the action of a substance and the hierarchy of their relative strength.

verses.sanskrit: रसादिसाम्ये यत्कर्म विशिष्टं तत्प्रभावजम् । दन्ती रसाद्यैस्तुल्यापि चित्रकस्य विरेचनी ॥२६॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 26 defines prabhava and gives classical examples where a substance acts differently despite similarity in rasa and related factors.

verses.sanskrit: मधुकस्य च मृद्वीका घृतं क्षीरस्य दीपनम् । इति सामान्यतः कर्म द्रव्यादीनां पुनश्च तत् ॥२७॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 27 defines prabhava and gives classical examples where a substance acts differently despite similarity in rasa and related factors.

verses.sanskrit: विचित्रप्रत्ययारब्धद्रव्यभेदेन भिद्यते । स्वादुर्गुरुश्च गोधूमो वातजिद्वातकृद्यवः ॥२८॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 28 introduces the distinction of substances formed from different causal elemental combinations and gives wheat and barley as the first example.

verses.sanskrit: उष्णा मत्स्याः पयः शीतं कटुः सिंहो न शूकरः ॥२८-१/२॥
verses.student_meaning: The concluding half-verse contrasts fish, milk, lion and boar to demonstrate how different causal formations can produce actions that do not follow merely from shared taste or heaviness.

sections.title: Dravya and Panchamahabhuta
sections.focus: Primacy of dravya, elemental composition and plurality of rasa/dosha associations.

sections.title: Mahabhuta-based Dravya Characteristics
sections.focus: Guna and action patterns of parthiva, apya, agneya, vayavya and nabhasa substances.

sections.title: Virya
sections.focus: Definitions, eightfold interpretation, ushna-shita classification and characteristic actions.

sections.title: Vipaka
sections.focus: Post-digestive transformation and principal vipaka categories.

sections.title: Dravya Karma and Relative Strength
sections.focus: Rasa, vipaka, virya and prabhava as determinants of action and their natural hierarchy.

sections.title: Prabhava
sections.focus: Specific action beyond ordinary rasa-virya-vipaka expectations.

sections.title: Vichitra Pratyayarabdha Dravya
sections.focus: How different causal elemental combinations produce distinctive properties and actions.

learning_outcomes: Define dravya and explain why rasa, guna, virya, vipaka and prabhava are described as dependent on it.
Explain the Panchamahabhuta basis of dravya.
Describe the characteristic qualities and actions associated with the five mahabhutas.
Explain the classical definitions and types of virya.
Define vipaka and explain its threefold classification.
Differentiate rasa, vipaka, virya and prabhava as determinants of dravya action.
Explain the natural hierarchy of strength among rasa, vipaka, virya and prabhava.
Define prabhava and explain its classical examples.
Explain the concept of vichitra-pratyayarabdha dravya using the chapter's examples.
exam_focus: Primacy of dravya and Panchamahabhuta composition.
Relative strength of rasa, vipaka, virya and prabhava.
Prabhava definition with Danti–Chitraka and Madhuka–Mridvika examples.
Vichitra-pratyayarabdha dravya and the final examples.

source_text.primary: Vāgbhaṭa Saṃhitā, Sūtrasthāna Chapter 9, TransLiteral and Wikisource
source_text.verification_note: Chapter 9 begins with the dravya definition and ends with verse 28 plus the traditional concluding half-verse. The next chapter is Rasabhediya. Text sequence and endpoint were cross-checked across independent classical-text presentations.

revision_summary: Compare the competing classical definitions of virya.
Remember the hierarchy rasa → vipaka → virya → prabhava when strengths are comparable.
Revise prabhava examples and the final vichitra-pratyayarabdha examples.
